Author: wyomingspopulation
Content:
Hey! My friend and I are high schoolers designing a hybrid buck-boost converter on GF180 (2.7–5.5V in, 5V out, ~500mA) and want to tape out on a quarter slot. A few questions:

Run 3 is too soon for us. Any idea when Run 4 will open and close, and will it have early bird pricing?
Any student discount? We’re self-funding.
The COB add-on needs the default pad ring. Is there any way to get COB bonding with a custom pad ring, even for an extra fee? Our power stage needs more power pads than the default ring has.
If we stick with the default ring: can we turn some of the signal pads into extra power/ground pads while keeping the same bond positions, so it still works with the breakout board?
Roughly how much current can one pad and one bond wire safely carry?

Thanks!

Author: sudonet
Content: a fellow high schooler, say? Would you be interested to work on the Hack Club ASIC instead? asic.hackclub.com

Author: sudonet
Content: It's basically tiny tapeout but for us lads

Author: sudonet
Content: not trying to market it, but I think you'd be interested. It's free, and is based on Tiny Tapeout GF180.

Author: sudonet
Content: and don't worry. there's COB packaging and funding for breakout boards. `:D

Author: sudonet
Content: however, i can tell you one thing about "student discounts": if there's free slots on the shuttle then you can theoretically get a free slot all to yourself. However, you won't get COB packaging for it, just bare die. Also, design must be public and open-source.

Author: sudonet
Content: I learnt it the hard way. 💀

Author: sudonet
Content: Also, run 4 will open some time in december, i'm pretty sure

Author: sudonet
Content: you can modify the padring to have extra vdd/vss pads as well in the same positions, i think

Author: sudonet
Content: But i can definitely tell you one can't get COB packaging with custom padring

Author: sudonet
Content: well... unless you do your own cob packaging. I'm sure @stuart can help you with that.

Author: wyomingspopulation
Content: Thanks, super helpful! Just to confirm: if we keep the default padring and only swap some signal pads to extra VDD/VSS in the same positions, does that still count as the default padring for wafer.space’s COB add-on?

Author: 246tnt
Content: That's fine. Those signals will have thinner traces though. ( The default pads for power use thicker trace and have decoupling caps on the COB itself).
